text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - Bund futures end solidly higher on Tuesday, following Treasuries higher to recover from steep losses earlier. Ranges seen Thursday between 100.75-101.50. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.38, up 0.23 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts settled higher on Tuesday, tracking meaty gains in U.S. Treasuries which were relieved employment cost index came in below 1.0 percent. Good cover at gilt auction had little immediate impact but bodes well for five-year tender Thursday. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-21/32, up 11/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - March bond futures climb as US data calms rate rise fears. Traders said some limited cash buying at long end. March PIBOR contract get boost at end from US fund. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 130.50 up 0.36 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures recovered from early weakness and returned to positive territory helped by dollar strength which is underpinning Btps despite a fall in Bunds, but today's Bot and Ctz auctions could limit rise. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 131.94 up 0.37 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries shave gain on Jan consumer confidence rise. Jan consumer confidence at 116.8 vs rev Dec 114.2. Treasuries, stocks, dollar up after Q4 ECI rose just 0.8 pct. ECI figure eased markets' inflation, Fed rate hike fears. Short-covering, fresh buying cited after 4 days of losses. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-26/32, up 1-01/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.85 percent.

JAPAN - Key March 10-year Japanese goverment bonds futures closed lower on Tuesday as new 10-year bonds auctioned today were slightly overpriced. Lowest accepted bid at 100.80 was higher than some bidders had expected. This slightly curbed investors' appetite for bonds, which carried record low 2.6 percent coupon.In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.35, down 0.30 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Expected rather than actual issuance was to the fore during a quiet Tuesday morning in the primary market. Osaka Gas will launch a $400 million deal on Wednesday. Kexim will set a $500 million medium-dated global bond. Turkey's expected 500 million mark Eurobond will have a seven-year maturity and be launched later this week Turkey will also issue a 500 billion Italian lire bond later in the first quarter of the year. Russian Uneximbank will award the mandate for a $100-200 million bond by the end of the week. A $300 million bond from DePfa was the main deal of the day.
